# Session Storage Separation

Decouple session storage from the shadow branch (`kspec-meta`) to eliminate sync conflicts, reduce shadow branch bloat, and support local-only or independently git-tracked sessions.

## Specs

```yaml
- title: Session Storage Modes
  slug: session-storage-modes
  type: requirement
  parent: "@session-model-evolution"
  tags: [session, storage, mvp]
  description: |
    Configurable session storage with two modes: local (default) and branch.
    Local mode writes to .kspec-sessions/ with no git tracking. Branch mode
    writes to .kspec-sessions/ backed by a named orphan branch for persistence.
    Shadow mode (sessions on kspec-meta) is legacy read-only — never written to.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-config
      given: |
        A kspec project with kynetic.yaml
      when: |
        sessions.storage is set to "local" or "branch"
      then: |
        Session operations use the configured storage mode.
    - id: ac-config-default
      given: |
        A kspec project with no sessions.storage in kynetic.yaml
      when: |
        A session operation runs
      then: |
        Defaults to "local" mode.
    - id: ac-config-invalid
      given: |
        sessions.storage is set to an unsupported value
      when: |
        kspec validates the manifest
      then: |
        Zod validation error with message indicating valid values (local, branch).
    - id: ac-local-mode
      given: |
        sessions.storage is "local" (or unconfigured)
      when: |
        A session is created, events appended, or session closed
      then: |
        Files are written to .kspec-sessions/{id}/ with no git operations.
    - id: ac-branch-mode
      given: |
        sessions.storage is "branch" with a branch name configured
      when: |
        A session is created or closed
      then: |
        Files are written to .kspec-sessions/ which is a git worktree
        on the configured orphan branch. Auto-commits on session lifecycle
        boundaries (create, close, stale cleanup, compact) but NOT on every event append.
    - id: ac-branch-name
      given: |
        sessions.storage is "branch"
      when: |
        sessions.branch is set (e.g., "kspec-sessions")
      then: |
        The orphan branch uses the configured name.
    - id: ac-branch-name-default
      given: |
        sessions.storage is "branch" with no sessions.branch set
      when: |
        Session branch is initialized
      then: |
        Default branch name is "kspec-sessions".
    - id: ac-no-event-commits
      given: |
        sessions.storage is "branch"
      when: |
        An event is appended to events.jsonl during active session
      then: |
        No git commit occurs. Events are committed in bulk at session close.
    - id: ac-sessions-dir
      given: |
        Any storage mode
      when: |
        Session operations resolve file paths
      then: |
        Sessions directory is .kspec-sessions/ at project root,
        separate from .kspec/ (which remains spec/task only).
    - id: ac-sessions-dir-autocreate
      given: |
        .kspec-sessions/ directory does not exist
      when: |
        A session create operation runs
      then: |
        The directory is created automatically (mkdir -p equivalent).
    - id: ac-gitignore
      given: |
        A kspec project
      when: |
        kspec init or kspec setup runs
      then: |
        .kspec-sessions/ is added to the project root .gitignore
        (not tracked on main branch regardless of storage mode).

- title: Legacy Session Migration
  slug: session-legacy-migration
  type: requirement
  parent: "@session-model-evolution"
  tags: [session, storage, migration, mvp]
  description: |
    Read-only fallback for sessions stored on the kspec-meta shadow branch
    (.kspec/sessions/) from before the storage separation. Provides migration
    path with deprecation timeline.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-read-fallback
      given: |
        A session ID is requested that does not exist in .kspec-sessions/
      when: |
        Any session read operation executes (get, list, log show, log search)
      then: |
        Falls back to reading from .kspec/sessions/ on kspec-meta.
        Result is returned normally — caller does not need to know the source.
    - id: ac-no-write
      given: |
        Legacy sessions exist in .kspec/sessions/ on kspec-meta
      when: |
        Any session write operation occurs (create, append, close, compact)
      then: |
        Writes always go to .kspec-sessions/, never to .kspec/sessions/.
    - id: ac-list-merge
      given: |
        Sessions exist in both .kspec-sessions/ and .kspec/sessions/
      when: |
        kspec session log list runs
      then: |
        Results include sessions from both locations, deduplicated by ID,
        with .kspec-sessions/ taking precedence for duplicates.
    - id: ac-deprecation-warning
      given: |
        A session is read from the legacy .kspec/sessions/ location
      when: |
        The read completes
      then: |
        A deprecation warning is emitted (stderr, not stdout) noting
        the legacy location. Warning includes guidance to run kspec session migrate.
    - id: ac-shadow-gitignore
      given: |
        kspec setup or kspec init runs
      when: |
        .kspec/sessions/ exists on kspec-meta
      then: |
        sessions/ is added to .kspec/.gitignore so no new session files
        are tracked on kspec-meta. Existing history is preserved in git.
    - id: ac-migration-copy
      given: |
        Legacy sessions exist in .kspec/sessions/
      when: |
        kspec session migrate runs
      then: |
        Copies session directories from .kspec/sessions/ to .kspec-sessions/.
        Does not delete originals.
    - id: ac-migration-idempotent
      given: |
        Some sessions already exist in .kspec-sessions/
      when: |
        kspec session migrate runs
      then: |
        Skips sessions that already exist in target.
        Reports count of migrated and skipped sessions.

- title: Session Storage Path Resolution
  slug: session-storage-path-resolution
  type: requirement
  parent: "@session-events"
  tags: [session, storage, refactor, mvp]
  description: |
    Centralized path resolution for session storage that all session
    operations use. Replaces hardcoded specDir/sessions paths with
    a resolver that accounts for storage mode configuration.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-resolver
      given: |
        Any session operation needs a file path
      when: |
        It calls the session path resolver
      then: |
        Returns paths rooted at .kspec-sessions/ (project root),
        not .kspec/sessions/.
    - id: ac-path-helpers
      given: |
        Existing path helpers (getSessionDir, getSessionEventsPath, etc.)
      when: |
        They resolve session paths
      then: |
        All use the new sessions root from the resolver.
    - id: ac-context
      given: |
        initContext() is called
      when: |
        Context is resolved
      then: |
        Context includes sessionsDir alongside specDir.
        sessionsDir points to .kspec-sessions/ at project root.
    - id: ac-cli-commands
      given: |
        A CLI session command accesses session data
      when: |
        It resolves session paths
      then: |
        Uses ctx.sessionsDir (not ctx.specDir) for all session file operations.
    - id: ac-daemon-routes
      given: |
        A daemon API route serves session data (/api/sessions/*)
      when: |
        It resolves session paths
      then: |
        Uses sessionsDir from project context for all session file operations.

- title: Session Branch Worktree Management
  slug: session-branch-worktree
  type: requirement
  parent: "@session-storage-modes"
  tags: [session, storage, git, post-mvp]
  description: |
    Git worktree management for the session branch mode. Creates and
    maintains an orphan branch with its own worktree at .kspec-sessions/.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-init
      given: |
        sessions.storage is "branch" and no session worktree exists
      when: |
        kspec init or kspec setup runs
      then: |
        Creates orphan branch with configured name (default "kspec-sessions"),
        adds worktree at .kspec-sessions/.
    - id: ac-commit-boundaries
      given: |
        sessions.storage is "branch"
      when: |
        Session lifecycle events occur (create, close, stale cleanup, compact)
      then: |
        Auto-commits to session branch at lifecycle boundaries only.
        Event appends during active sessions are NOT committed individually.
    - id: ac-sync
      given: |
        sessions.storage is "branch" and remote tracking is configured
      when: |
        Daemon shadow sync runs
      then: |
        Session branch syncs independently from kspec-meta.
        Sync failures on one branch do not affect the other.
    - id: ac-status
      given: |
        sessions.storage is "branch"
      when: |
        kspec shadow status runs
      then: |
        Reports health of both kspec-meta and session branch worktrees.
    - id: ac-repair
      given: |
        Session worktree is broken or disconnected
      when: |
        kspec shadow repair runs
      then: |
        Repairs session worktree independently from kspec-meta worktree.

- title: Remove Shadow Commits for Sessions
  slug: session-remove-shadow-commits
  type: requirement
  parent: "@session-storage-modes"
  tags: [session, storage, refactor, mvp]
  description: |
    Remove all shadowAutoCommit calls related to session operations.
    Sessions no longer dirty the kspec-meta worktree.
  acceptance_criteria:
    - id: ac-invocation-end
      given: |
        An agent invocation ends (completed, timed_out, failed, aborted)
      when: |
        closeSession() is called in invocation.ts
      then: |
        No shadowAutoCommit is called for the session.
        Task state changes (if any) still commit to kspec-meta normally.
    - id: ac-stale-cleanup
      given: |
        Stale session auto-abandon runs
      when: |
        Session metadata is updated to abandoned
      then: |
        Commit goes to session branch (if branch mode) or nowhere (if local).
        No commit to kspec-meta.
    - id: ac-no-sync-conflict
      given: |
        Dispatch engine creates sessions while daemon syncs shadow branch
      when: |
        Periodic shadow sync runs shadowPull on kspec-meta
      then: |
        No conflict occurs because session files are not in the kspec-meta worktree.

  parent: "@session-model-evolution"

Decouple session storage from the shadow branch (`kspec-meta`) to eliminate sync conflicts, reduce shadow branch bloat, and support local-only or independently git-tracked sessions.

─── Description ───
Automated task loop using ACP protocol. Runs claude-agent-acp agent in a loop to process kspec tasks autonomously with full event logging and streaming output.

─── Acceptance Criteria ───
  [ac-1]
    Given: ready tasks exist
    When: kspec ralph is run with --max-loops N
    Then: spawns ACP agent and runs up to N iterations
  [ac-2]
    Given: no ready tasks exist
    When: kspec ralph is run
    Then: command exits with message indicating no ready tasks
  [ac-3]
    Given: a loop iteration starts
    When: agent picks and works on a task
    Then: agent uses task start, task note, and task complete commands per working procedure
  [ac-4]
    Given: a loop iteration ends with work still in progress
    When: agent cannot complete the task in one iteration
    Then: agent commits WIP, adds note documenting progress, and task remains in_progress for next iteration
  [ac-5]
    Given: a loop iteration completes (task done or WIP)
    When: there are uncommitted changes
    Then: agent commits the changes with appropriate message
  [ac-6]
    Given: --dry-run flag is provided
    When: kspec ralph --dry-run is run
    Then: shows the prompt that would be sent without executing agent
  [ac-7]
    Given: agent returns error during iteration
    When: the error occurs
    Then: retry the iteration up to max-retries times before failing the loop
  [ac-8]
    Given: multiple consecutive iterations fail after all retries
    When: the failure count reaches max-failures threshold
    Then: the loop exits early with an error message
  [ac-9]
    Given: --adapter flag is provided
    When: kspec ralph --adapter <id> is run
    Then: uses specified adapter (default claude-agent-acp)
  [ac-10]
    Given: session starts
    When: agent spawns
    Then: creates new session with ULID and logs session.start event
  [ac-11]
    Given: agent streams updates
    When: updates arrive
    Then: displays streaming output to CLI and logs to session events
  [ac-12]
    Given: prompt is sent
    When: iteration starts
    Then: logs prompt.sent event with full prompt content
  [ac-13]
    Given: session ends
    When: loop completes or errors
    Then: logs session.end event with status and triggers commit
  [ac-14]
    Given: a loop iteration starts
    When: building prompt for the agent
    Then: creates a fresh ACP session so each iteration has a clean context window
  [ac-15]
    Given: --focus flag is provided with instructions
    When: building prompt for each iteration
    Then: includes the focus instructions prominently in the prompt, emphasizing they apply to all iterations
  [ac-16]
    Given: ralph loop is running
    When: checking for available tasks (ready or in_progress)
    Then: only considers tasks with automation: eligible status; both ready tasks and in_progress tasks are filtered by automation eligibility
  [ac-17]
    Given: ralph loop is running with --restart-every N (N > 0)
    When: iteration completes and iteration number is divisible by N
    Then: agent process is killed and respawned to prevent memory buildup
  [ac-18]
    Given: --restart-every 0 is specified
    When: iterations complete
    Then: agent process is never restarted (maintains single agent instance)
  [ac-19]
    Given: ralph loop iteration completes
    When: determining whether to continue looping
    Then: loop continues if automation:eligible ready tasks OR automation:eligible in_progress tasks exist; exits with message when neither remain
  [ac-20]
    Given: processPendingReviewTasks completes during iteration
    When: checking for loop continuation
    Then: uses freshly gathered task context (not stale from iteration start) to detect tasks that became ready due to dependency unblocking
  [ac-21]
    Given: User runs kspec ralph with --tasks @ref1,@ref2
    When: task selection runs each iteration
    Then: only the explicitly listed tasks are considered for work, regardless of automation eligibility of other tasks; exits when all listed tasks are completed or blocked

    Given: A terminal/run tool request produces large stdout or stderr output
    When: Ralph handles the terminal/run request
    Then: Ralph streams stdout and stderr to per-session artifact files under .kspec/sessions/{session}/tool-output/ instead of accumulating unbounded output in memory
  [ac-23]
    Given: A terminal/run command completes after producing output
    When: Ralph sends the tool response and renders tool output
    Then: The response includes bounded previews and metadata (stdout_path, stderr_path, stdout_bytes, stderr_bytes, preview_truncated) while preserving access to full output via artifact files
  [ac-24]
    Given: --iteration-timeout <minutes> is provided (default: 20)
    When: ralph runs an iteration
    Then: the entire task-work and reflect prompt phase is bounded by that timeout; defaults to 20 minutes if not specified
  [ac-25]
    Given: --iteration-timeout receives a non-positive or non-numeric value
    When: ralph starts
    Then: exits immediately with an error indicating --iteration-timeout must be a positive number of minutes
  [ac-26]
    Given: an iteration timeout fires while agent is still running
    When: the timeout expires
    Then: logs iteration.timeout event with iteration/attempt/timeout metadata and applies existing retry/failure escalation logic
  [ac-27]
    Given: Agent streams many updates rapidly during an iteration
    When: Session update events are logged
    Then: Updates are queued and written sequentially with backpressure — concurrent appendEvent calls do not accumulate unbounded in-flight promises
